title: Graceful tenant eviction and lightweight fallback path for burst 5xx
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a 2025-02-08 escalation from two customers, the Hosted API experienced a 20-minute window of elevated 5xxs and timeouts concentrated in a regional front-door. Root cause analysis points to retry amplification combined with aggressive KV cache eviction under memory pressure: repeated client retries caused a feedback loop where inflight requests forced higher KV churn, increasing tail latency and downstream model OOMs on serving hosts. The immediate mitigation (short-term) gated tenant retries and increased circuit thresholds. This ticket implements a medium-term fix: a graduated tenant eviction and lightweight-fallback fastpath to prevent global degradation while preserving availability for healthy tenants.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New tenant-score-based admission prevents bursty tenants from triggering host-level KV thrashing; 2) Lightweight fastpath serves a reduced-memory model variant or shorter max-length with p95 latency under threshold; 3) SDK surfaces server-side suggested retry windows and idempotency token guidance; 4) Canary rollout to 10% tenants with auto-rollback on >2x 5xx for canary cohort; 5) Observability dashboards show KV eviction rate down 60% and p99 latency restored within SLOs during synthetic burst tests.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: We evaluated two approaches: (A) aggressive host-wide admission that immediately quarantines noisy tenants, which minimizes blast radius but risks false positives and customer impact; (B) graduated eviction (chosen) that scores tenant behavior over a short sliding window and progressively limits resources (rate cap -> reduced model -> full quarantine). Trade-off: chosen approach is more complex but reduces mistaken quarantines. We will still keep an emergency fast quarantine kill-switch for incidents.
implementation_plan: 1) Implement tenant scoring service (lightweight, stateless rollup) in front-door to track retries, error-rate, request concurrency; 2) Admission controller enforces graduated actions: throttle -> reduced-quality fastpath -> quarantine; 3) Fastpath: route to quantized / shorter-context model variant with lower KV footprint and lower token budget; 4) Add idempotency and retry-hint headers in API responses and update SDK guidance; 5) Add metrics and Grafana dashboards; 6) CI load test and chaos scenario; 7) Canary rollout and monitor.
updates: 2025-02-10 Maya Chen: Triage call notes — customers A and B reported elevated 5xx and timeouts with retries. Initial hotfix applied: edge-side soft-throttle and temporary rate caps. Agreed to build graduated eviction + fastpath rather than blunt host quarantine.

2025-02-11 Liam O'Rourke: PoC for tenant scoring (in-memory sliding window) validated on staging; synthetic replay of customer traffic reproduced KV eviction spike. PoC PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8920

2025-02-12 Priya Singh (SRE): Observability plan reviewed. Added new Grafana panels: per-tenant 5xx rate, KV eviction rate, GPU queue depth, fastpath hit-rate. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-api/tenant-5xx
2025-02-13 Diego Ramirez (SDK): SDK patch to support 'Retry-After-Suggested' and idempotency token guidance drafted. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/776

2025-02-14 Liam O'Rourke: Implementation branch merged for admission controller (feature-flagged). Canary plan created: start at 10% tenant-surface in us-west, watch p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, KV eviction. Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-420489+Eviction+and+Fastpath
testing_and_rollback_plan: Staging: run synthetic burst tests (varying retry rates) and ensure KV eviction and p99 latency meet thresholds. Canary: 10% tenants in us-west for 4 hours; automatic rollback triggers: >2x baseline 5xx rate or sustained p99 latency increase >50ms. Rollback steps: flip feature-flag, reapply soft-throttle policy, notify customers. Post-canary: progressive 25% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics stable.
postmortem_and_followups: Post-deploy tasks: 1) Complete incident postmortem and notify impacted customers (owner: Maya Chen); 2) Plan longer-term runtime improvements: KV eviction backpressure in kernel scheduler and smarter batching heuristics (follow-up ticket); 3) Update SLAs and runbook to include this graduated eviction path; 4) Add automated tenant health scoring to alerting with runbook links.
customer_communication_plan: Notify impacted customers with technical summary and mitigations applied. For canary rollout, proactively message large tenants with recommended SDK updates (idempotency token). Prepare FAQ and support playbook for front-line support.
notes: This ticket targets reducing blast radius from tenant retry storms without hard quarantines. It intentionally pairs runtime changes with SDK guidance so clients reduce harmful retry patterns. Coordinate with PM and Design for UX for error responses and retry hints.
